feedback: Frank's confession follows the previously visible contradiction between the claimed barrier and the open preview stand. It uses his architectural habits and failed promises in a way that sounds personal, and the closing concern about his name on the plans works emotionally. His actual taking of poison and dosing of the glass are admissions, not an additional physical clue; those acts were inferable possibilities before voting but not independently established. Monet and Chip maintain their priorities even when conceding dishonesty, which makes their innocence speeches credible. The solution feels earned as a best-supported narrative deduction, although an investigator would still want corroboration of Frank's handling. It introduces no new essential mechanism or source.
